_campaign_notes.why_not_the_vendor_repo: ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-9B-GGUF is first-party but ships no quant below Q4_K_M, so a Q8/Q4/Q2 ladder cannot be built from it. Every third-party conversion checked (mradermacher, AtomicChat, prithivMLmods) reads block_count 32, nextn_predict_layers None, params 8,953,803,264 -- they DROP the model's multi-token-prediction layer. The vendor and protoLabsAI both read block_count 33, nextn_predict_layers 1, params 9,197,093,888. The 243,290,624-param difference predicts a 0.487 GB BF16 file-size gap against 0.490 GB observed. Mixing repos would put a different ARCHITECTURE at the two ends of the quant ladder, so all three arms come from one lineage (rule 3, rule 30).
_campaign_notes.drafter: protoLabsAI is the only source that also ships a separate MTP head (mtp-head/mtp-Ornith-1.5-9B-head-Q8_0.gguf, 2.43 GB), which is what puts 'drafter' in inspect-model.py's capabilities list. Ornith-1.0-9B had no draft head anywhere, so speculative decoding is an axis this campaign can run and the 1.0 campaign could not.
_campaign_notes.ladder_order: Q8_0 -> Q4_K_M -> IQ2_M, highest quality first (rule 6 ranks by perplexity and the ladder order is the comparison order).
_campaign_notes.conditional_fourth_arm: IQ4_XS (5.45 GB) is NOT on the roster. It earns a run only if Stage 1's pruning gate or the Stage 6 ladder shows Q4_K_M measurably trailing Q8_0, which would make the IQ-versus-K-quant question at 4-bit worth an answer. Recorded here so it is a decision and not an omission (over-measurement guard).
